mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the matrix-enforced Permitted-implies-allowed rule lets Alloy invent a Permitted operation whose caller's role lacks the matrix entry, which is exactly what LeastPrivilege (and the FR-011 specialisation) must refuse.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Permitted and (op.caller.role -> op.kind) not in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the at-most-one-audit-entry-per-operation constraint lets Alloy create two distinct AuditEntries pointing at the same Operation, which the AppendOnly assertion must catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.op = ae2.op }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the obligation to write an audit row for every served LookupRecord access lets Alloy invent a permitted/denied access with no audit row — exactly the SC-001/SC-002 failure mode.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = LookupRecord and op.authenticated = True and some op.outcome and (no ae: AuditEntry | ae.op = op) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the byte-equivalence rule lets Alloy create a Denied LookupRecord whose response is not the canonical 404 — directly violating FR-007's no-leakage guarantee.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InfoLeakViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = LookupRecord and op.outcome = Denied and op.byteEquivNotFound = False }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the care-team membership check lets Alloy permit a clinician's read of a patient they have no membership for — the exact SC-010 violation the ownership pattern exists to detect.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamGatingViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = LookupRecord and op.outcome = Permitted and (no m: CareTeamMembership | m.clinician = op.caller and m.patient = op.targetPatient) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the auth-boundary rule lets Alloy invent an unauthenticated operation that nonetheless writes an audit row / returns content — the exact FR-001 / SC-004 failure surface.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthBoundaryViolation { some op: Operation, ae: AuditEntry | op.authenticated = False and op.kind = LookupRecord and ae.op = op and some op.caller }
